title: Load the code before restoring off-code coupling and preserve every error branch
statement: Let bare space=C plus D, dim(C)=c fixed, C=ker(A), A|D>=a*I,a>0, bounded bath Q>=B*I and final W=(W_C,W_D). Independently gate W_D and apply all of D(t)=W(t)^*QW(t), including cross-blocks. Stage I with W_D=0 loads C using the full-code scalar-ramp bound epsilon1=[2(c+1)*ell_C+5*ell_C^2]/(B*T1), ell_C<=c*pi/2. Stage II freezes W_C and restores W_D(t)=tau(t)*W_D; V_C=((I+W_C^*W_C)^-1/2,0,-W_C*(I+W_C^*W_C)^-1/2)^T is fixed and H_tau*V_C=-B*V_C. Final isometry error is at most epsilon1, for an arbitrary untouched reference.

requires: A supplied protected-code decomposition and known W_C/W_D; independently gate the off-code source and calibrate the full matrix counterterm throughout both stages.
Closed coherent unitary dynamics with admissible controls and actual source/readout preparation; the code/bath Stage-I model satisfies the full-code theorem.

assumptions: No native endpoint-only implementation or bounded switching/work/noise cost is supplied. Mathematical code invariance does not acquire the selective controls.
The complementary final gap may be small; ideal code preservation is exact, while finite control errors require a separate inclusive bound.
costs: Pay T1 and every off-code switching/cross-counterterm/precision cost during T2. No extra IDEAL isometry error is added by Stage II; this is not zero physical work or a hardware speed guarantee.
contract.units: hbar=1; B*T1 dimensionless, error is isometry norm, delta H is energy and its time integral is dimensionless; tau is a normalized source gate.
contract.obstruction: Realize or falsify off-code source selectivity and full compensation in a constrained microscopic controller.

body: Here ell_C=int_0^1 max_positive_lambda sqrt(lambda)/(1+eta^2*lambda) d eta for the eigenvalues of W_C^*W_C; if W_C=0, Stage I is stationary with zero error. During Stage I the penalized D sector is decoupled, so the full-code theorem applies to C plus bath; it does not require a gap in the final completed proper-code controller. During Stage II R_tau=(W_C,tau*W_D,I) obeys R_tau*V_C=Rprime_tau*V_C=0 and A*V_C=0. Thus both (H_tau+B)*V_C and partial_tau(H_tau)*V_C vanish, giving only the known phase under any well-defined restoration schedule. Unitarity preserves the norm of all actual Stage-I leakage/error branches, so no conditioning or error amplification is omitted. The fixed code can survive ideal arbitrarily fast restoration even when the complementary gap collapses. In the explicit trap W_C=sqrt(lambda),W_D=lambda, a relative error epsilon_c in the sole cross-counterterm leaves residual |epsilon_c|*Q*|tau|*lambda^(3/2)/sqrt(1+lambda). Order1/lambda relative accuracy controls a fixed instantaneous residual, not automatically integrated gate error. A sufficient perturbation bound charges integral||delta H(t)||dt. The repair uses strictly stronger controls than a single shared envelope.
